record.title: Shahriari and Yu's conjecture for forbidden copies of $Y_k$ and $Y'_k$
record.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power, and let $\mathrm{La}_q(n,\{Y_k,Y'_k\})$ denote the maximum size of a family of subspaces of an $n$-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{F}_q$ containing neither $Y_k$ nor $Y'_k$ as a subposet. Let $\Sigma_q(n,k)$ denote the corresponding sum of the $k$ largest Gaussian binomial coefficients. **Shahriari and Yu's conjecture.** For $k\geq 1$ and $n\geq k+1$, 

$$
\mathrm{La}_q(n,\{Y_k,Y'_k\})=\Sigma_q(n,k).
$$

The conjecture is a vector-space analogue of a forbidden-poset theorem in the Boolean lattice; the cited paper proves this result using the $q$-analogue of the Lubell–Yamamoto–Meshalkin inequality.
record.source_name: Jimeng Xiao and Casey Tompkins, “On forbidden poset problems in the linear lattice”, arXiv:1905.09246 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.09246

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of May 2019); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Dorbec et al.'s power domination bound for connected regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected $r$-regular graph of order $n$, with $r\ge 3$, and let $k\ge 1$. Write $\gamma_{p,k}(G)$ for the minimum cardinality of a $k$-power dominating set of $G$. Assume that $G\not\cong K_{r,r}$. **Dorbec et al.'s conjecture.** Then

$$
\gamma_{p,k}(G)\le \frac{n}{r+1}.
$$

This conjecture extends known upper bounds for $k$-power domination in regular graphs by removing the claw-free hypothesis. Its status is unclear from the supplied text.
record.source_name: Hangdi Chen, Changhong Lu and Qingjie Ye, “Generalized power domination in claw-free regular graphs”, arXiv:1905.11655 (2020).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1808.02613](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.02613).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.11655

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2019). “When $l\ge 4$, the conjecture is still open.”

record.title: Claw-free regular graph power domination conjecture
record.statement:
Let $l\ge 1$ and $k\ge l$ be integers, and let $G$ be a connected claw-free $(k+l+1)$-regular graph of order $n$. Let $\gamma_{p,k}(G)$ denote the minimum cardinality of a $k$-power dominating set of $G$. **Claw-free regular graph power domination conjecture.** Then

$$
\gamma_{p,k}(G)\le \frac{n}{k+l+2},
$$

and this bound is tight. The construction $C_{k,t}$ described in the source shows tightness for the relevant parameters. The conjecture is stated to remain open when $l\ge 4$.
record.source_name: Hangdi Chen, Changhong Lu and Qingjie Ye, “Generalized power domination in claw-free regular graphs”, arXiv:1905.11655 (2020).
record.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.11655

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2019). “When $l\ge 4$, the conjecture is still open.”

record.title: Existence of a dfs measure that is not finitely approximated
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a theory, let $\mathcal{U}$ be a monster model of $T$, and let $\mu\in\mathfrak{M}_x(\mathcal{U})$ be a Keisler measure. A measure is **dfs** if it is definable and finitely satisfiable. **Existence conjecture.** There is a theory $T$ and a Keisler measure $\mu\in\mathfrak{M}_x(\mathcal{U})$ such that $\mu$ is dfs but not finitely approximated.

The examples preceding this conjecture exhibit dfs measures that are not finitely approximated in related settings, while also noting that the relevant measure need not extend to a global dfs measure. The conjecture asks whether such a measure exists for some theory in general.
record.source_name: Gabriel Conant and Kyle Gannon, “Remarks on generic stability in independent theories”, arXiv:1905.11915 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.11915

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2019).

record.title: Il'yuta's monotone-cycle conjecture for Coxeter–Dynkin diagrams
record.statement: Assume $n\equiv2\pmod 4$. Let $D$ be a Coxeter–Dynkin diagram, with vertices given by a distinguished basis and edge weights $\langle\delta_i,\delta_j\rangle$. A **monotone cycle** is a sequence of vertices $(\delta_{i_1},\ldots,\delta_{i_k})$ with $i_1<\cdots<i_k$, in which each $\delta_{i_j}$ is connected to $\delta_{i_{j+1}}$, with indices taken cyclically. Let ${\mathcal D}$ denote the collection of such diagrams, and let the modality be the modality of the singularity. **Il'yuta's monotone-cycle conjecture.** The minimum over all $D\in{\mathcal D}$ of the smallest number of edges that must be deleted so that $D$ contains no monotone cycles is equal to the modality of the singularity. The conjecture was disproved by counterexamples for bimodal singularities.
record.source_name: Wolfgang Ebeling, “Distinguished bases and monodromy of complex hypersurface singularities”, arXiv:1905.12435 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.12435

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of May 2019); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The conjectured subquadratic bound for parent-identifying schemes
record.statement:
Let $t\ge 4$ be an integer and define

$$
w=\left\lfloor\left(\frac{t}{2}+1\right)^2\right\rfloor.
$$

For a $t$-parent-identifying scheme with block size $w$ on a $v$-point ground set, let $I_t(w,v)$ be its maximum number of blocks. **Subquadratic IPPS conjecture.** One has

$$
I_t(w,v)=o(v^2).
$$

The conjecture seeks a subquadratic upper bound in the first parameter range not handled by the graph argument described in the source: for $t\ge 4$, the chosen value of $w$ exceeds $2t$, so $t$ edges do not determine enough points to form a $w$-subset. The authors suggest that hypergraphs or more elaborate analyses may remove this obstacle; the conjecture is presented as unresolved.
record.source_name: Yujie Gu, Minquan Cheng, Grigory Kabatiansky and Ying Miao, “Probabilistic Existence Results for Parent-Identifying Schemes”, arXiv:1906.01031 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.01031

record.title: Superspace Vandermonde model for the Delta operator
record.statement:
Let $n=k+r$ and let ${\mathbf a}=(k-1,k-1,\dots,k-1)$ be a length-$r$ sequence whose entries are all $k-1$. Let $\mathcal V_n({\mathbf a})$ be the smallest subspace containing the corresponding superspace Vandermonde and closed under the indicated partial derivatives and polarization operators, and let ${\mathrm {grFrob}}(\mathcal V_n({\mathbf a});q,t)$ be its doubly graded Frobenius image. **Superspace Vandermonde conjecture.** One has

$$
{\mathrm {grFrob}}(\mathcal V_n({\mathbf a});q,t)=\Delta'_{e_{k-1}}e_n.
$$
 The statement proposes a representation-theoretic model for $\Delta'_{e_{k-1}}e_n$; the source reports that its specialization at $t=0$ is proved by Theorem~, while Zabrocki's corresponding conjecture remains open even at $t=0$.
record.source_name: Brendon Rhoades and Andrew Timothy Wilson, “Vandermondes in superspace”, arXiv:1906.03315 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.03315

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2019). “Theorem proves Conjecture in the case $t = 0$; Zabrocki's conjecture is open even in the case $t = 0$.”

record.title: Width-two conjecture for the first missing linear extension number
record.statement:
For each positive integer $n$, let $M_2(n)$ be the smallest positive integer that is not the linear extension number of a width-$2$ poset. **Width-two conjecture.**

$$
M_2(n)=\exp(\Omega(n)).
$$

The motivation is that the posets constructed earlier to obtain small linear extension numbers all have width $2$; the conjecture asserts that this restricted class asymptotically achieves the same exponential scale as the unrestricted first missing value.
record.source_name: Noah Kravitz and Ashwin Sah, “Linear extension numbers of n-element posets”, arXiv:1906.06036 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.06036

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2019).

record.title: The edge-addition conjecture for rooted phylogenetic networks
record.statement:
Let $N$ be a rooted phylogenetic network on leaf set $X$. The quantities $\ell(N)$ and $e(N)$ measure, respectively, the tree-based proximity of $N$ and the minimum number of directed edges that must be added to make $N$ tree-based. **Edge-addition conjecture.** There exists a set of directed edges that can be added to $N$ to turn it into a tree-based rooted phylogenetic network on leaf set $X$. Furthermore,

$$
\ell(N)\le e(N)\le 2\ell(N).
$$

The conjecture asserts both that every rooted phylogenetic network can be made tree-based by adding directed edges and that the required number of additions is at most twice its tree-based proximity. The preceding example shows that the unrooted equality $e(N)=\ell(N)$ does not extend to rooted networks, since there $e(N)=2>1=\ell(N)$.
record.source_name: Mareike Fischer and Andrew Francis, “How tree-based is my network? Proximity measures for unrooted phylogenetic networks”, arXiv:1906.06163 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.06163

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2019).

record.title: Gupta's co-density conjecture for multigraph cover index
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a multigraph. Its cover index $\xi(G)$ is the maximum number of pairwise disjoint edge covers of $G$, and its minimum degree is $\delta(G)$. Define the co-density by

$$
\Phi(G)=\min\left\\{\frac{2|E^+(U)|}{|U|+1}: U\subseteq V,\ |U|\geq 3\text{ and odd}\right\\},
$$

where $E^+(U)$ consists of the edges with at least one end in $U$. **Gupta's co-density conjecture.** Every multigraph $G$ satisfies

$$
\xi(G)\geq \min\\{\delta(G)-1,\\,\lfloor \Phi(G) \rfloor\\}.
$$

The conjecture is the cover-packing counterpart of the Goldberg–Seymour edge-coloring conjecture. Its validity would constrain the cover index to two possible values relative to the fractional cover index; the paper reports only approximate bounds as known.
record.source_name: Yan Cao, Guantao Chen, Guoli Ding, Guangming Jing and Wenan Zang, “On Gupta's Co-density Conjecture”, arXiv:1906.06458 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.06458

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2019).

record.title: Gupta's characterization conjecture for the cover-index lower bound
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a multigraph, with minimum degree $\delta(G)$ and maximum edge multiplicity $\mu(G)$. Suppose that $\delta(G)$ cannot be expressed in the form

$$
2p\mu(G)-q
$$

for any integers $p$ and $q$ satisfying $q\geq 0$ and $p>\mu(G)+\left\lfloor (q-1)/2\right\rfloor$. **Gupta's characterization conjecture.** Then

$$
\xi(G)\geq \delta(G)-\mu(G)+1.
$$

Gupta proposed this as a complete characterization of the parameter values for which equality in the general lower bound $\xi(G)\geq \delta(G)-\mu(G)$ cannot occur. The paper presents the statement as a conjecture and does not report a resolution.
record.source_name: Yan Cao, Guantao Chen, Guoli Ding, Guangming Jing and Wenan Zang, “On Gupta's Co-density Conjecture”, arXiv:1906.06458 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.06458

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2019).

record.title: The maximal 3-gamma_c-vertex critical graph Hamiltonian connectivity conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a **maximal $3$-$\gamma_{c}$-vertex critical graph**, and let $\alpha$, $\kappa$, and $\delta$ denote its independence number, connectivity, and minimum degree, respectively. Assume

$$
\alpha=\kappa=\delta.
$$

**Hamiltonian connectivity conjecture.** Then $G$ is either the $5$-cycle $C_{5}$ or hamiltonian connected.

Together with the preceding result that every such graph with $\kappa<\delta$ is hamiltonian connected, this would establish that every maximal $3$-$\gamma_{c}$-vertex critical graph is either $C_{5}$ or hamiltonian connected. The conjecture concerns the remaining case $\alpha=\kappa=\delta$ and is presented as the needed step toward that conclusion.
record.source_name: Norah Almalki and Pawaton Kaemawichanurat, “Inequalities of Independence Number, Clique Number and Connectivity of Maximal Connected Domination Critical Graphs”, arXiv:1906.07619 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.07619

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2019).

record.title: Generalized Nagao conjecture for hyperelliptic Jacobians
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a hyperelliptic curve defined over $\mathbb{Q}(T)$ whose Jacobian $J_{\mathcal{X}}$ has no subvariety defined over $\mathbb{Q}$. For an integer $t$, let $a_{\mathcal{X}_t}(p)=p+1-\#\mathcal{X}_t(\mathbb{F}_p)$ and define

$$
A_{\mathcal{X},1}(p)=\frac{1}{p}\sum_{t=0}^{p-1}a_{\mathcal{X}_t}(p).
$$

**Generalized Nagao conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{P \to \infty} \frac{1}{P} \sum_{p \leq P} -A_{\mathcal{X},1}(p) \log p=\operatorname{rank} J_{\mathcal{X}}(\mathbb{Q}(T)).
$$

The conjecture is proposed as the rank-detecting generalization of Nagao's conjecture for hyperelliptic Jacobians. The paper uses it conditionally to construct high-rank examples, and no resolution status is supplied here.
record.source_name: Trajan Hammonds, Seoyoung Kim, Benjamin Logsdon, Álvaro Lozano-Robledo and Steven J. Miller, “Rank and Bias in Families of Hyperelliptic Curves via Nagao's Conjecture”, arXiv:1906.09407 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.09407

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2019).

record.title: No optimal planar integral point set with a unit edge for at least six points
record.statement: Let $\mathfrak{M}(2,n)$ denote planar integral point sets with $n$ points, and call $M$ **optimal** when it attains the minimum possible diameter among sets in $\mathfrak{M}(2,n)$. **No-unit-edge optimality conjecture.** Every set $M\in\mathfrak{M}(2,n)$ with $n\geq 6$ such that $|M_1M_2|=1$ for some $M_1,M_2\in M$ is not optimal. The claim extends the observed existence of optimal sets containing distance $1$ for $n=3,4,5$; the source gives higher-point facher optimal sets as motivation, but leaves the assertion open.
record.source_name: Nikolai Avdeev, “On existence of integral point sets and their diameter bounds”, arXiv:1906.11926 (2019).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.11926

record.title: Neumann–Lara–Škrekovski conjecture on the dichromatic number of planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, and let $\vec{\chi}(G)$ denote the maximum, over all orientations of $G$, of the minimum number of acyclic colour classes in a vertex colouring. **Neumann–Lara–Škrekovski conjecture.** Every planar graph satisfies

$$
\vec{\chi}(G) \leq 2.
$$

This is the directed analogue of the Four-Colour Theorem and is equivalent, as stated in the source, to the assertion that every planar digraph is $2$-colourable. The source does not provide evidence of a resolution.
record.source_name: Raphael Steiner, “A Note on Graphs of Dichromatic Number 2”, arXiv:1907.00351 (2019).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1401.2213](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.2213), [arXiv:1110.4900](https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.4900).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.00351

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

record.title: Aldous–Fill spectral-gap conjecture for regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected $k$-regular graph on $n$ vertices. Its **spectral gap**, or algebraic connectivity, is the second smallest eigenvalue of its Laplacian matrix. Equivalently, for regular graphs it is $k$ times the second smallest eigenvalue of the normalized Laplacian.

**Aldous–Fill spectral-gap conjecture.** The spectral gap of a connected $k$-regular graph on $n$ vertices is at least

$$
(1+o(1))\frac{2k\pi^2}{3n^2},
$$

and the bound is attained for at least one value of $k$.

This is an equivalent spectral-gap formulation of the conjecture on maximum relaxation time. The paper proves it for cubic graphs, while the general assertion remains open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: M. Abdi, E. Ghorbani and W. Imrich, “Regular Graphs with Minimum Spectral Gap”, arXiv:1907.03733 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.03733

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

record.title: The maximum-independent-sets conjecture for k-chromatic ℓ-connected graphs with k at most ℓ
record.statement:
Let $G^*$ denote the graph characterized in the paper as the extremal $n$-vertex $k$-chromatic 
$$
-connected graph, and let $i(G)$ be the number of independent sets in $G$. **The maximum-independent-sets conjecture.** Let $3 k $ and $n 2$. If $G$ is an $n$-vertex $k$-chromatic
$$
-connected graph, then

$$
i(G) i(G^*).
$$

Theorem characterizes $G^*$ for large $n$, and this conjecture proposes that the same extremal graph works throughout the stated range.
record.source_name: John Engbers, Lauren Keough and Taylor Short, “Independent Sets in n-vertex k-chromatic, -connected graphs”, arXiv:1907.03913 (2019).

record.statement:

record.title: Beck–Fiala conjecture for regular hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a $t$-regular hypergraph, meaning that every vertex belongs to exactly $t$ hyperedges. For a hypergraph $\mathcal{H}=(V,E)$, let $\operatorname{disc}(\mathcal{H})$ denote its discrepancy, the minimum over all $\pm1$ colorings of the maximum absolute signed edge sum.

**Beck–Fiala conjecture.** For a $t$-regular hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$, we have

$$
\operatorname{disc}(\mathcal{H})=O(\sqrt{t}).
$$

This is one of the central open problems in discrepancy theory; the paper’s main spectral bound gives an $O(\sqrt{t}+\lambda)$ estimate, but does not establish the conjectured bound for general $t$-regular hypergraphs.
record.source_name: Aditya Potukuchi, “A spectral bound on hypergraph discrepancy”, arXiv:1907.04117 (2020).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1811.01491](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.01491).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.04117

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2019). “One of the most interesting open problems in discrepancy theory is what is commonly known as the Beck-Fiala conjecture, regarding the discrepancy of general $t$-regular hypergraphs.”

record.title: Koolen–Yang integrability conjecture for graphs with smallest eigenvalue at least -3
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an unsigned graph with smallest eigenvalue at least $-3$. For a natural number $c$, call $G$ **$c$-integrable** if there exists an integer matrix $N$ such that $c(A-\floor{\lambda_{min}}I)=NN^{T}$, where $A$ is the adjacency matrix of $G$ and $\lambda_{min}$ is its smallest eigenvalue.

**Koolen–Yang conjecture.** There exists a constant $c$ such that every unsigned graph $G$ with smallest eigenvalue at least $-3$ is $c$-integrable.

This conjecture asks for a uniform integrability bound extending known results for graphs with smallest eigenvalue at least $-3$ and sufficiently large valency. The source presents it as an open direction related to extending those results to signed graphs.
record.source_name: Francesco Belardo, Sebastian M. Cioabă, Jack H. Koolen and Jianfeng Wang, “Open problems in the spectral theory of signed graphs”, arXiv:1907.04349 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.04349

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2019). “This conjecture was also recently proved by Rizzolo .”

record.title: Gregory's signing conjecture for irregular graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a nontrivial graph, let $\Delta$ be its largest vertex degree, and let $\sigma$ be a signature of $G$. Write $\rho(G,\sigma)$ for the spectral radius of the signed adjacency matrix associated with $\sigma$.

**Gregory's conjecture.** There exists a signature $\sigma$ such that

$$
\rho(G,\sigma)<2\sqrt{\Delta-1}.
$$

This is an irregular-graph variant of the regular signing conjecture. The source says that Gregory considered this variant but gives no evidence of a resolution.
record.source_name: Francesco Belardo, Sebastian M. Cioabă, Jack H. Koolen and Jianfeng Wang, “Open problems in the spectral theory of signed graphs”, arXiv:1907.04349 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.04349

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2019). “This conjecture was also recently proved by Rizzolo .”

record.title: Non-smash-product conjecture for the generalized symmetry bialgebroid
record.statement:
Let $X$ be the finite set underlying the function algebra $C(X)$, and let $H$ be the smallest subalgebra of $C(X \times X \times X \times X)$ containing $C(X)$ and the set $H_0$ of functions satisfying the three displayed conditions in the construction above. The resulting $H$ is a left bialgebroid over $C(X)$ whose action on $C(X)$ lifts to universal one forms. **Non-smash-product conjecture.** $H$ is not of the form

$$
C(X)\# Q
$$

for any Hopf algebra $Q$ acting on $C(X)$. This asserts that the generalized symmetry bialgebroid constructed here cannot in general be represented as a smash product by an acting Hopf algebra.
record.source_name: Suvrajit Bhattacharjee, Indranil Biswas and Debashish Goswami, “Generalized symmetry in noncommutative (complex) geometry”, arXiv:1907.04673 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.04673

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

record.title: Brown–Erdős–Sós and Alon–Shapira conjecture on sparse hypergraph exponents
record.statement:
Let $f_r(n,v,e)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $r$-graph on $n$ vertices such that every set of $v$ vertices spans at most $e-1$ edges. For fixed integers $r>k\ge 2$ and $e\ge 3$, consider $f_r(n,er-(e-1)k+1,e)$. **Brown–Erdős–Sós and Alon–Shapira conjecture.** As $n\to\infty$,

$$
n^{k-o(1)}<f_r(n,er-(e-1)k+1,e)=o(n^k).
$$

The upper bound is known in the stated parameter range, and several lower-bound cases are known; the smallest unresolved case is whether $f_3(n,7,4)=o(n^2)$.
record.source_name: Chong Shangguan and Itzhak Tamo, “Degenerate Turán densities of sparse hypergraphs”, arXiv:1907.04930 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.04930

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2019).

record.title: Caro–Hegarty–Morrison quadratic-order conjecture for arithmetic-progression zero sums
record.statement:
Let $r$ and $s$ be fixed positive integers. For a function $f:[n]\to\{-r,s\}$ with $f([n])=0$, let $M(r,s,k)$ denote the minimum threshold such that every sufficiently large $n$ forces a zero-sum $k$-term arithmetic progression. **Caro–Hegarty–Morrison's conjecture.** There are positive constants $c_1=c_1(r,s)$ and $c_2=c_2(r,s)$ such that

$$
c_1k^2\le M(r,s,k)\le c_2k^2.
$$

Thus the threshold for zero-sum arithmetic progressions has quadratic order in $k$. Existing results give superlinear lower bounds and quadratic upper bounds, but the matching quadratic lower bound remains open.
record.source_name: Alec Sun, “Zero-sum subsequences in bounded-sum \-r,s\-sequences”, arXiv:1907.06623 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.06623

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2019).

record.title: Order-independent termination of the reversible-realization heuristic
record.statement: Let a kinetic differential equation be represented by a polynomial vector field, and consider the heuristic that repeatedly pairs monomial reactant vectors with reaction vectors to construct a reversible realization. **Order-independent termination conjecture.** If there exists a reversible realization, then this process terminates, independently of the order of the actions, and necessarily produces one of the reversible realizations, although the realization may depend on the order of the steps. The claim concerns whether this heuristic always succeeds when a reversible realization exists; no resolution is given in the source.
record.source_name: G. Craciun, M. D. Johnston, G. Szederkényi, E. Tonello, J. Tóth and P. Y. Yu, “Realizations of kinetic differential equations”, arXiv:1907.07266 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.07266

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

record.title: Outerplanar graph polygon-chain determination conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a bi-connected outerplanar graph. Let $G^*$ be its inner dual, and let $P_1\cup\cdots\cup P_t$ be the polygon chain decomposition of $G$ corresponding to the maximal path decomposition of $G^*$. Write $\tau(P_i)$ for the number of spanning trees of $P_i$, and let $\mu(G)$ denote the minimum number of generators of the sandpile group $S(G)$. **Polygon-chain determination conjecture.** The quantity $\mu(G)$ is determined by the numbers

$$
\tau(P_1),\ldots,\tau(P_t).
$$

For polygon flowers, the analogous assertion follows from the paper's results; the conjecture extends this phenomenon to all bi-connected outerplanar graphs, and its resolution is not given in the source.
record.source_name: Haiyan Chen and Bojan Mohar, “The sandpile group of a polygon flower”, arXiv:1907.08450 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.08450

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

record.title: Recursive muffin-algorithm value conjecture
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a 3M-DAP that is not a 0-problem, and let $P'$ be the smaller 3M-DAP obtained from $P$ by one application of the recursive algorithm. Let $g(P)$ denote the size of the smallest piece in the solution produced by that algorithm.

**Recursive value conjecture.** For any 3M-DAP $P$ that is not a 0-problem,

$$
g(P)=g(P').
$$

The source says that it proves this conjecture in the subsequent analysis. Therefore its status is solved.

record.title: Malle–Robinson conjecture on simple modules in blocks of finite groups
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a finite group. For subgroups $N\unlhd K\subseteq H$, call $K/N$ a **section** of $H$. Define the **sectional $\ell$-rank** $s(H)$ to be the maximum rank of an elementary abelian $\ell$-section of $H$. For a block $B$ of $H$, let $l(B)$ denote the number of irreducible Brauer characters in $B$. If $B$ is an $\ell$-block of $H$ with defect group $D$, then

**Malle–Robinson conjecture.**

$$
l(B)\leq \ell^{s(D)}.
$$

This conjecture bounds the number of simple modules in a block by the sectional $\ell$-rank of its defect group. The supplied text gives no evidence of a resolution.

record.title: Minimum-weight MIPPR word conjecture for minimal PPRIC codes
record.statement: Let $r$, $s$, and $L$ be nonnegative integers with $L\geqslant 2s+r+1$, and let $C\subseteq {\cal W}_s$ be a minimal $(L,s,r)$ PPRIC code. An **MIPPR word** is a word associated with $C$ having the minimum possible intersection property described for PPRIC codes. **Minimum-weight MIPPR word conjecture.** Any MIPPR word of minimum weight in $C$ has weight $r+3$. By the preceding lemma, every MIPPR word has weight at least $r+3$; the conjecture asserts that this lower bound is attained for minimal PPRIC codes. The paper presents it as an intriguing conjecture motivating constructions and lower bounds, with no resolution given.

record.title: Berger–Wang conjecture for modified EGZ constants in powers of $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})$
record.statement:
For positive integers $n=2^k$ and $d\geq 1$, let $s'_n(G)$ denote the modified Erdős-Ginzburg-Ziv constant of a finite abelian group $G$. Let $\ell$ be the smallest integer such that $\ell\geq 2^d$ and $\ell\nmid n$. **Berger–Wang conjecture.** One has

$$
s'_n\left((\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^d\right)=2^d n-\ell+1.
$$

The conjecture is presented as an open problem concerning modified EGZ constants in higher-dimensional groups; no resolution is given in the source.

record.title: Type-one tree complement conjecture for multiplicity bipartition
record.statement: Let $T=S^k_{m,n}$ be the tree formed by taking a path on $k$ vertices and adding $m$ leaves to one endpoint and $n$ leaves to the other, where $kin\{2,3,4\}$ and $m,n>1$. Write $q(G)$ for the minimum number of distinct eigenvalues of a graph $G$, and $MB(G)$ for its multiplicity bipartition. **Type-one tree complement conjecture.** Then $q(\overline{T})=2$ and $MB(\overline{T})=3$. The conjecture concerns a family of complements of type-one trees and asserts both the two-eigenvalue property and the specified multiplicity bipartition; the surrounding discussion presents these as open problems.

record.title: Join conjecture with maximum multiplicity parameter
record.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs such that $q(G)=q(H)=2$, with $MB(G)=k_1$ and $MB(H)=k_2$, and suppose that the quantities denoted in the source by $\mrr+(G)$ and $\mrr+(H)$ satisfy $\mrr+(G)=k_1$ and $\mrr+(H)=k_2$. **Join maximum-multiplicity conjecture.** Then $q(G\vee H)=2$ and $MB(G\vee H)=k$, where

$$
k=\max\{k_1,k_2\}.
$$
 This is a proposed generalization of the preceding join inequality; the custom notation $\mrr+$ is not defined in the supplied context.

record.title: Jiang–Polyanskii conjecture for infinite spectral radius order
record.statement:
Fix $\alpha\in(0,1)$, let $N_\alpha(d)$ be the maximum number of equiangular lines in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with common angle parameter $\alpha$, and set

$$
\lambda=\frac{1-\alpha}{2\alpha}.
$$

For a real $\lambda>0$, let $k(\lambda)$ be the smallest number of vertices of a graph whose spectral radius is exactly $\lambda$, with $k(\lambda)=\infty$ if no such graph exists.

**Jiang–Polyanskii conjecture.** If $k(\lambda)=\infty$, then

$$
N_\alpha(d)=d+O_\alpha(1).
$$

The paper explains that its main theorem gives only $N_\alpha(d)=d+O_\alpha(d/\log\log d)$ in this case, while the conjectured bounded excess over $d$ remains open. It also notes that the conjecture had been verified except when $\lambda$ is a totally real algebraic integer that is largest among its conjugates.

record.title: Independent-set bound for graphs excluding a clique minor
record.statement:
Let $t$ be a positive integer, let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph, and let $\alpha(G)$ denote the size of its largest independent set. **Independent-set bound for clique-minor-free graphs.** If $G$ does not contain $K_{t+1}$ as a minor, then

$$
\alpha(G)\geq \frac{n}{t}.
$$

This bound would follow from Hadwiger's conjecture, since every $n$-vertex graph has chromatic number at least $\lceil n/\alpha(G)\rceil$. Duchet and Meyniel proved the bound within a factor of $2$, and subsequent work improved the factor; the exact bound remains open in general.

record.title: Convexity conjecture for the pendulum time map
record.statement: Let $T_B(z,\phi)$ be the time map defined in the paper for parameters $z$ and $\phi$, with $z\in(0,2)$ and $\phi\in(0,\frac{\pi}{2})$. **Convexity conjecture.** For each $\phi\in(0,\frac{\pi}{2})$, the function $z\mapsto T_B(z,\phi)$ is convex. The authors report convincing numerical evidence for the positivity of the quantity governing the second derivative, but were unable to prove it; establishing this convexity would yield the existence of a single minimum of the time-map graph.

record.title: Extremal number conjecture for matching blow-ups of complete bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $K_{s,t}$ be the complete bipartite graph with $s\leq t$, let $p\geq 3$, and let $\mathcal{M}(K^{p+1}_{s,t})$ denote the matching blow-up family used in the paper. Let $h(n,1,s)$ and $f(t-1,t-1)$ be the functions defined in the paper. **Matching blow-up extremal-number conjecture.** If $n\geq s+2t$ and $p\geq 3$, then

$$
\emph{ex}(n,\mathcal{M}(K^{p+1}_{s,t}))=h(n,1,s)+f(t-1,t-1)-\left\lceil\frac{s-1}{2}\right\rceil+i,
$$

where $i=1$ if $s=t$ is even and $i=0$ otherwise. The conjecture concerns the exact extremal number for the matching blow-up of $K_{s,t}$, which the paper does not determine in its theorem; its resolution is not supplied here.

record.title: Revised conjecture for the non-monochromatic extremal function
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a given graph, and let $g(n,G)$ denote the maximum number of edges not contained in any monochromatic copy of $G$ in a $2$-edge-coloring of $K_n$. Let $\emph{ex}(n,G)$ denote the extremal number of $G$. **Revised non-monochromatic extremal conjecture.** If $n$ is sufficiently large, then there exists a constant $h_G$ depending on $G$ such that

$$
g(n,G)=\emph{ex}(n,G)+h_G.
$$

This revises the earlier equality conjecture after the paper exhibits counterexamples to it. The asserted bounded additive correction is left open in the supplied text.

record.title: Maximum-row-degree exponent conjecture for zero-one matrices
record.statement:
Let $t\geq 2$ be a positive integer, and let $A$ be a zero-one matrix such that every row of $A$ contains at most $t$ $1$-entries. **Maximum-row-degree exponent conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{ex}(n,A)=n^{2-\frac{1}{t}+o(1)}.
$$

This is presented as a strengthening of results proved in the paper and remains open. The authors note that even the case of matrices corresponding to cycles is of interest.

record.title: Heil's minimum-volume conjecture for bodies of given thickness
record.statement: Let $d$ be a prescribed thickness, and consider convex bodies in three-dimensional space with thickness $d$. The **Heil body** is the convex hull of six circular arcs of radius $d$, centered at the midpoints of the edges of a regular tetrahedron of edge length $d\sqrt{2}$, together with the four vertices of a rescaled tetrahedron of edge length $d(2\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2})/3$. **Heil's conjecture.** The Heil body is the minimum-volume three-dimensional body in the class of convex bodies with given thickness. The conjecture concerns the unresolved minimum-volume problem for convex bodies of prescribed thickness; the source gives no resolution.

record.title: Campi–Colesanti–Gronchi conjecture for bodies of revolution with constant brightness
record.statement: Let $b$ be a prescribed brightness, and consider convex bodies of revolution in three-dimensional space with constant brightness $b$. **Campi–Colesanti–Gronchi conjecture.** The body constructed by Blaschke has minimum volume among all convex bodies of revolution with constant brightness $b$. This is the rotationally symmetric version of the minimum-volume problem for constant brightness; the source gives no resolution.
